name: Sodium pyruvate
description: Sodium pyruvate (CAS 113-24-6 ) is the sodium salt form of pyruvic acid, offering greater stability and handling convenience than the free acid. It functions as a metabolic substrate, buffering agent, and cell-protective additive across food, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and biotech applications. In cell culture and fermentation media, it serves as a direct carbon source that supports cell viability and reduces oxidative stress in sensitive mammalian cell lines. Food and nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it as a metabolic energy substrate in sports nutrition products. These dietary supplements often target endurance and weight management. In cosmetic formulations, it acts as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in moisturizers, serums, and anti-aging products where moisture retention directly affects performance claims. Pharmaceutical researchers also use it as a cryoprotective additive in parenteral formulations and as a stabilizing excipient in freeze-dried biologics. This versatility makes it a critical component in modern medical and laboratory research environments. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include cell culture-grade, often provided as a sterile-filtered solution at 100 mM, as well as USP and food-grade specifications for various industrial requirements. Bulk quantities are available for industrial biotech and food manufacturing, with smaller pack sizes offered for laboratory and pharmaceutical compounding use.
